lesson.text: Quick memory: in a relief print, which parts print? (The raised parts.) In grade 3 you built sculptures to walk round. Today: sculptures that stand out from a wall.
A sculpture in the round stands free: you can walk all the way round it. A relief is carved or built on a flat background, like a wall, and is seen from the front.
In low relief, the shapes stand out only a little from the background. The heads on coins are low relief.
In high relief, the shapes stand out a lot, with some parts almost free of the wall.
In sunken relief, the shapes are cut into the surface. Ancient Egyptians carved sunken reliefs on temple walls, where the bright sun made their edges cast strong shadows.
Famous reliefs: the marble frieze of the Parthenon in Athens is about 2,500 years old. Lorenzo Ghiberti's golden bronze doors in Florence were made almost 600 years ago.
Make a relief by adding (press clay onto a flat slab) or by taking away (carve into clay or plaster). Light from one side shows a relief best: its shadows make the shapes stand out.
Try it in the world: build a relief on a wall in your world: blocks sticking out one block make low relief, more make high relief. Look at it when the sun is low and watch the shadows.

exercises.prompt: What kind of sculpture is this?
exercises.hint: From the side: how far does it stand out from the wall?
exercises.explain: It stands out only a little: low relief.

exercises.prompt: You can walk all the way round a sculpture in the round.
exercises.explain: True: it stands free, so it has no back against a wall.

exercises.prompt: Which of these has a low relief design?
exercises.hint: Which one has a picture that stands out a tiny bit?
exercises.explain: The head on a coin stands out a little: low relief.

exercises.prompt: Match each kind of sculpture to what it is like.
exercises.hint: Low and high tell you how far it stands out.
exercises.explain: Low: a little. High: a lot. Sunken: cut in. In the round: stands free.

exercises.prompt: What kind of relief is this?
exercises.hint: From the side: does it stand out, or is it cut in?
exercises.explain: The shape is cut into the wall: sunken relief.

exercises.prompt: What kind of relief is this?
exercises.hint: From the side: how far does it stand out?
exercises.explain: It stands out a long way from the wall: high relief.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: in the round, or a relief?
items: a pattern carved on a wall
exercises.hint: Can you walk all the way round it?
exercises.explain: Statues and chess pieces stand free. Coins, door panels and wall carvings are reliefs.

exercises.prompt: Ancient Egyptians often carved sunken reliefs.
exercises.explain: True: they carved many sunken reliefs, whose edges cast strong shadows in the bright sun.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps of a clay relief in order.
exercises.hint: The flat background comes first; drying comes last.
items: Roll out a flat clay slab
exercises.explain: Slab, design, shapes, details, then let it dry.

exercises.prompt: Why is a relief easiest to see with light from one side?
choices: its shadows make the shapes stand out
light from the side is brighter
exercises.explain: Light from one side makes shadows next to the raised shapes, so they stand out.

exercises.prompt: Carving into a clay slab makes a relief by…
exercises.hint: Does carving put clay on, or take it off?
exercises.explain: Carving cuts into the clay and takes some away, so the design is made by taking away. Pressing clay shapes on would be adding.

exercises.prompt: The Parthenon's frieze is about 2,500 years old and Ghiberti's doors almost 600. About how many years older is the frieze?
exercises.hint: Take the smaller number from the bigger one.

exercises.prompt: In high relief, the shapes stand out only a tiny bit.
exercises.explain: False: that is low relief. In high relief, the shapes stand out a lot.

exercises.prompt: In your world, you build a face on a wall that sticks out almost as far as it is wide. What kind of sculpture is it?
exercises.hint: It is still joined to the wall. How far does it stand out?
exercises.explain: It is on a wall and stands out a lot: high relief.

exercises.prompt: Sort these ways of making a relief: adding, or taking away?
exercises.hint: Does it put material on, or take it off?
exercises.explain: Pressing clay, gluing card and building blocks add. Carving and cutting take away.

exercises.prompt: Order them by how far they stand out from the wall, the least first.
exercises.hint: One is cut into the wall, and one does not need a wall at all.
exercises.explain: Sunken relief is cut into the surface, so it does not stand out at all. Low relief stands out a little and high relief a lot. A sculpture in the round stands free of any wall.
